spec.description: The tide gauges of the Americas on the IOC (UNESCO) network, from the Arctic to Tierra del Fuego, over the last 24 hours: each port’s tide over its own day on a map and in a north-to-south grid, with play to watch it travel along the coast, filters by range, coast and area, and the minute-by-minute height of the port you click.

options.content:
### Where the data comes from

- **Tide gauges**: the [Sea Level Station Monitoring Facility](https://www.ioc-sealevelmonitoring.org/) of UNESCO’s Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC), run by VLIZ (Belgium). It gathers in real time, mostly over the WMO’s Global Telecommunication System, the readings of the national networks: INOCAR’s in Ecuador, SHOA’s in Chile, NOAA’s in the United States, and so on for each country. They are **raw data, with no quality control**, read from its v1 web service, which needs no key. Each network arrives with its own delay: from minutes to a few hours.
- Taken are the tide gauges of the Americas (from the Arctic to Tierra del Fuego, with Galápagos, Juan Fernández and the Caribbean; without Hawaii or Polynesia) that measure in metres, gave a reading in the last 24 hours and have at least 12 hours of them. Left out are the DART buoys, which measure in the open ocean, flat sensors (a tide under 5 cm is a sensor that stopped), and series with a jump from one quarter-hour to the next of more than half their tide (a real tide moves a tenth of its range at most: that is a step or a spike of the sensor). Where two codes share a site (a backup sensor), the one with more readings stays.

### How it is computed

- **Each quarter-hour**, the median of its readings. Spikes go first: readings more than five median deviations from the station’s median of the day.
- **Each gauge measures against a zero of its own**, so heights are not compared, but each port’s tide over its own day: **low water** is the 2nd percentile of its 24 hours and **high water** the 98th (so a stray reading does not set them). The **height over low water** is the height minus its low water, and the **height over its day** goes from 0 at low water to 1 at high water: the colour of the map and of the grid. The **tide range** is high water minus low water, and is the size of each dot.
- **The coast**: north of the Arctic Circle, the Arctic; the Pacific by country (Chile, Peru, Ecuador, El Salvador), west of 100° W, and in Central America and Colombia by the line between their two coasts; the rest, the Atlantic, with the Caribbean and the Gulf of Mexico.
- **Times are UTC.** The minute-by-minute series reads the same raw readings of the port, with the same spike filter.

### How it works

The server reads each tide gauge (about 360 requests, one per station) through Pacha’s gateway, which keeps a copy of each and renews it in the background once it is a quarter of an hour old; it reduces the readings to quarter-hours and hands them to your browser (Chaski). The filters, play, the map and the grid (Mosaic) are answered there, without going back to the server. **Reload the page** to bring in new readings.

spec.description: The newest 15-minute reading of all the tide gauges. Each network arrives with its own delay: from minutes to a few hours.
spec.title: Latest data

spec.rawSql:
-- Every 15-minute reading of every gauge (has_reading = 1: the grid cells with one), oldest
-- first, so a port shows the latest one the time window holds on top. The time, range, coast
-- and area filters reach the map from the Mosaic selection (mosaicSelection) and filter it on
-- the GPU; the port search is here.
SELECT code, station, country, coast, latitude, longitude, time,
       above_low, fraction, tide_range, trend
FROM $tides
WHERE has_reading = 1 AND contains(lower(station), lower(${search:sqlstring}))
ORDER BY time, code

spec.rawSql:
-- The clicked gauge minute by minute, from the same copy the gateway keeps for the dataset,
-- with the same spike filter and its height over the day's low water.
-- One GET per file and no HEAD: the gateway renews its copies in the background, and a copy
-- renewed between DuckDB's HEAD and GET came back cut at the old length, malformed JSON that
-- failed the whole read. The setting outlives this query on the shared connection.
SET force_download = true;
SET VARIABLE window_start = date_trunc('hour', now()::TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL 24 HOUR;
SET VARIABLE url = coalesce((
  SELECT 'http://feeds/ioc/data/' || Code || '/' || sensor || '/' || strftime(getvariable('window_start')::DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') || '.json'
  FROM read_json('http://feeds/ioc/stations.json', format = 'array')
  WHERE Code = $gauge
  LIMIT 1
), 'http://feeds/ioc/data/none/none/2000-01-01.json');
WITH readings AS (
  SELECT stime AS time, slevel
  FROM read_json(getvariable('url'), columns = {slevel: 'DOUBLE', stime: 'TIMESTAMP', sensor: 'VARCHAR'}, format = 'array')
  WHERE stime >= getvariable('window_start') AND slevel IS NOT NULL
),
centre AS (SELECT median(slevel) AS m FROM readings),
clean AS (
  SELECT time, slevel FROM readings, centre
  WHERE abs(slevel - m) <= 5 * greatest((SELECT median(abs(slevel - m)) FROM readings, centre), 0.05)
)
SELECT time, round(slevel - (SELECT quantile_cont(slevel, 0.02) FROM clean), 3) AS "Above low water"
FROM clean
ORDER BY time

Tides of the Americas — the IOC tide gauges

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: the tide gauges of the Americas on the IOC's Sea Level Station Monitoring
-- Facility (VLIZ), as 15-minute medians of the 24 hours before the current quarter-hour,
-- through the gateway, which keeps a copy of each station refreshed every quarter of an hour
-- (one request per station).
--
-- Each gauge measures against a zero of its own, so every port is also put on a scale of its
-- own day: above_low is the height over its low water (the 2nd percentile of the day, so a
-- stray reading does not set it), and fraction goes from 0 at low water to 1 at high water.
-- Readings more than five median deviations from the station's median are spikes, and go.
-- Kept: gauges in metres, heard from in the last day, with 12 hours of readings or more, a tide
-- of 5 cm or more (a flat line is a sensor out) and no jump between two quarter-hours of more
-- than half of it (a real tide moves a tenth of its range at most: that is a step or a spike);
-- one per site; no DART buoys.
-- The window: the 96 quarter-hours before the current one, so every day has the same columns.
-- One GET per file and no HEAD: the gateway renews its copies in the background, and a copy
-- renewed between DuckDB's HEAD and GET came back cut at the old length, malformed JSON that
-- failed the whole read. The setting outlives this query on the shared connection.
SET force_download = true;
SET VARIABLE window_end = time_bucket(INTERVAL 15 MINUTE, now()::TIMESTAMP);
SET VARIABLE window_start = getvariable('window_end') - INTERVAL 24 HOUR;
SET VARIABLE stations = (
  SELECT list({code: Code, sensor: sensor, name: trim(Location), country_ioc: countryname, latitude: Lat, longitude: Lon})
  FROM read_json('http://feeds/ioc/stations.json', format = 'array')
  WHERE Lon BETWEEN -180 AND -26 AND Lat > -60 AND NOT (Lat < 50 AND Lon < -130)
    AND units = 'M' AND lasttime >= getvariable('window_start') AND Location NOT ILIKE 'DART%'
);
SET VARIABLE urls = (
  SELECT list('http://feeds/ioc/data/' || s.code || '/' || s.sensor || '/' || strftime(getvariable('window_start')::DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') || '.json')
  FROM (SELECT unnest(getvariable('stations')) AS s)
);
WITH stations AS (
  SELECT unnest(s) FROM (SELECT unnest(getvariable('stations')) AS s)
),
readings AS (
  SELECT regexp_extract(filename, '/ioc/data/([^/]+)/', 1) AS code, stime, slevel
  FROM read_json(getvariable('urls'), columns = {slevel: 'DOUBLE', stime: 'TIMESTAMP', sensor: 'VARCHAR'},
                 format = 'array', filename = true)
  WHERE stime >= getvariable('window_start') AND stime < getvariable('window_end') AND slevel IS NOT NULL
),
centre AS (SELECT code, median(slevel) AS m FROM readings GROUP BY code),
spread AS (
  SELECT code, any_value(m) AS m, median(abs(slevel - m)) AS mad
  FROM readings JOIN centre USING (code) GROUP BY code
),
quarters AS (
  SELECT code, time_bucket(INTERVAL 15 MINUTE, stime) AS time, median(slevel) AS level
  FROM readings JOIN spread USING (code)
  WHERE abs(slevel - m) <= 5 * greatest(mad, 0.05)
  GROUP BY ALL
),
jumps AS (
  SELECT code, max(abs(level - before)) AS jump
  FROM (SELECT code, level, lag(level) OVER w AS before, time - lag(time) OVER w AS step
        FROM quarters WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY code ORDER BY time))
  WHERE step = INTERVAL 15 MINUTE
  GROUP BY code
),
ports AS (
  SELECT code, quantile_cont(level, 0.02) AS low_water, quantile_cont(level, 0.98) AS high_water,
         count(*) AS n, max(time) AS latest, any_value(jump) AS jump
  FROM quarters JOIN jumps USING (code) GROUP BY code
  HAVING count(*) >= 48 AND quantile_cont(level, 0.98) - quantile_cont(level, 0.02) >= 0.05
     AND any_value(jump) <= 0.5 * (quantile_cont(level, 0.98) - quantile_cont(level, 0.02))
),
-- One gauge per site: where two codes share a place (a backup sensor), the one with more readings.
sites AS (
  SELECT p.*, s.* EXCLUDE (code)
  FROM ports p JOIN stations s USING (code)
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY round(s.latitude, 2), round(s.longitude, 2) ORDER BY p.n DESC, p.code) = 1
),
named AS (
  SELECT *,
    regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(name, '_([A-Z]{2})$', ', \1'), '_', ' ', 'g'), ',(\S)', ', \1', 'g') AS station,
    CASE country_ioc
      WHEN 'USA' THEN 'United States' WHEN 'Puerto Rico; U.S.A.' THEN 'Puerto Rico' WHEN 'Perú' THEN 'Peru'
      WHEN 'Brasil' THEN 'Brazil' WHEN 'Panamá' THEN 'Panama' WHEN 'Haïti' THEN 'Haiti' WHEN 'UK' THEN 'United Kingdom'
      WHEN 'Bermudas' THEN 'Bermuda' WHEN 'Dominica island' THEN 'Dominica' WHEN 'Trinidad & Tobago' THEN 'Trinidad and Tobago'
      WHEN 'Bahamas/Bahama Islands' THEN 'Bahamas' WHEN 'British Virgin Islands; U.K.' THEN 'British Virgin Islands'
      WHEN 'Saint Vincent & Grenadines' THEN 'Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' ELSE country_ioc END AS country,
    -- The ocean the gauge is on: north of the Arctic Circle, the Arctic; the Pacific coasts by
    -- country, and across Central America by the line between its two coasts; the rest of the
    -- Americas is Atlantic (Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico included). Countries as the IOC names them.
    CASE
      WHEN latitude > 66.5 THEN 'Arctic'
      WHEN country_ioc IN ('Chile', 'Perú', 'Ecuador', 'El Salvador') THEN 'Pacific'
      WHEN longitude < -100 THEN 'Pacific'
      WHEN country_ioc = 'Mexico' AND latitude < 17.3 AND longitude < -92 THEN 'Pacific'
      WHEN country_ioc = 'Guatemala' AND latitude < 15 THEN 'Pacific'
      WHEN country_ioc = 'Honduras' AND latitude < 14.5 THEN 'Pacific'
      WHEN country_ioc = 'Nicaragua' AND longitude < -85 THEN 'Pacific'
      WHEN country_ioc = 'Costa Rica' AND (longitude < -83.5 OR latitude < 9.5) THEN 'Pacific'
      WHEN country_ioc = 'Panamá' AND latitude < 9.2 THEN 'Pacific'
      WHEN country_ioc = 'Colombia' AND longitude < -77 AND latitude < 7.5 THEN 'Pacific'
      ELSE 'Atlantic'
    END AS coast
  FROM sites
),
-- The row of each gauge in the heatmap: the Pacific, then the Atlantic, then the Arctic, each from
-- north to south, with seven empty rows between them for the coast's name.
lanes AS (
  SELECT *, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY k, latitude DESC, code) + 7 * k AS lane
  FROM (SELECT *, CASE coast WHEN 'Pacific' THEN 0 WHEN 'Atlantic' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS k FROM named)
),
-- Every gauge at every quarter-hour of the window, has_reading = 0 where it has none: the heatmap
-- draws one cell per gauge and quarter-hour and leaves those clear, and every day has the same
-- 96 columns. The map and the counts keep has_reading = 1.
grid AS (
  SELECT unnest(generate_series(getvariable('window_start'), getvariable('window_end') - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE, INTERVAL 15 MINUTE)) AS time
)
SELECT s.code, s.sensor, s.station, s.country, s.coast, s.latitude, s.longitude, g.time,
       CASE WHEN q.level IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS has_reading,
       round(q.level, 3) AS level,
       round(greatest(q.level - s.low_water, 0), 3) AS above_low,
       round(least(greatest((q.level - s.low_water) / (s.high_water - s.low_water), 0), 1), 3) AS fraction,
       round(s.high_water - s.low_water, 2) AS tide_range,
       CASE WHEN q.level > lag(q.level) OVER w THEN 'rising' WHEN q.level < lag(q.level) OVER w THEN 'falling' END AS trend,
       s.latest, s.lane
FROM lanes s CROSS JOIN grid g
LEFT JOIN quarters q ON q.code = s.code AND q.time = g.time
WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY s.code ORDER BY g.time)
ORDER BY g.time, s.code
